# FDG9145

> DO use `ReadOnlyMemory<T>` in place of `ReadOnlySpan<T>` for parameters when the purpose of the constructor or method is to store a reference to the buffer.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 9.12 Operating on Buffers.

## How it is checked

- Check: judgment
- Automatic fix: no
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test none
- Status: verified

The text has no body; the body of FDG9146 gives the reason for both. Not machine-checkable: whether the purpose of a member is to store a reference to the buffer is intent. A ReadOnlySpan<T> can be stored only in a ref struct (a class field of a span type is CS8345 in a probe with SDK 10.0.402), whose constructor may keep it, as FDG9139 allows. Span<T> and Memory<T> types need .NET Core 2.1 or later, or the System.Memory package on .NET Framework and .NET Standard 2.0 (see FDG9137).
